messages.subject: Semilandmark difficulties
parts:
Hi All,

(Lou and Emma, many thanks for your helpful comments on my last post)

I am new to R and Geomorph (although practicing daily), I'm having a lot of trouble getting digitsurface to place semilandmarks (sLM) evenly across specimens and I'm wondering if someone might be able to offer any advice.   

I'm attempting to plot sLM across scanned objects (lithic cores) that are largely amorphous and lack any homologous reference points for plotting traditional LM. My scans were generated through a Nextengine scanner on HD, so all meshes contain points in the 1-4 million range. In order to remove some of the redundant points and create a more uniform mesh, I've sub-sampled meshes to 50k through a uniform function in GeoMagic, which creates a more even point grid and then were remeshed.

I've selected a specific (target) specimen for the buildtemplate function. I've tried hand-plotting LM through digit.fixed (N= 20), I've also tried sub-sampling the target mesh to 50 points and saved as a .csv with X,Y,Z values (then imported as a matrix) for use with the "fixed=" parameter in buildtemplate (i realize this is likely incorrect in its use). In any case, either method gives me strange results. I've attached pics of the results. The first pic (digit.fixed.result) shows sLM clumping in places after using digit.fixed, even though the vertices and triangles in the mesh are evenly spaced (as best as I could with such dense point clouds). The second pic (fixed=.result) shows the results of the matrix used in the "fixed=" parameter, where all LMs are clumped to one end of the scan.

I understand that the digitsurface function works through downsampling meshes and using a 'nearest neighbor' algorithm. Given that my meshes are uniformly down-sampled, might the density (approx. 30-50k) of points affect sLM placement?

My other thought is the lack of homologous points to use with digit.fixed, would that have an effect?  

I'm using RStudio. My coding skills are novel at best, but here's my workflow using the .csv import method. *For self-plotting LM using digit.fixed, I simply use buildtemplate(Core10, fixed=20, 200) & digitsurface(Core1, fixed=20)

#Import PLYs:
Core10 <- read.ply("C:/Users/MCaruana/Documents/R/Geomorph/C/C10.ply")
Core1 <- read.ply("C:/Users/MCaruana/Documents/R/Geomorph/C/C1.ply")

#Convert .csv to matrix (I imported a .csv file through the import function in the 'Environment' window):
lm <- as.matrix(LM.csv)

#Build semi-landmark template:
buildtemplate0(Core10, fixed=lm, 200)

#Place semi-landmarks:
digitsurface(Core1, fixed=lm)

Any advice would be much, much appreciated!!

Matt

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: Semilandmark difficulties
parts:
First off I must stress that the digitizing capabilities of geomorph are not meant to be suitable for all cases - we cannot preempt the types of structures people might want to digitize and as such, the methods we have implemented are not universal. However, this isn't a problem only with geomorph - this is the case for all 3D digitizing software. Issues with sliding smeilandmarks have been discussed for a decade at least, beginning with problems of digitizing the parietal crest of gorillas in Edgewarp as far as I know.

Ok, that aside, I think the problem is that as you say yourself, your specimen lack homologous points (fixed landmarks). For the function to work correctly (see below on how the function works), you must have equivalent, positionally or biologicaly homologous fixed landmarks. The "strange results" you are seeing are due to the template being made based on the set of 20 fixed points you have set on the first specimen, and these not corresponding to those on the second, where you fitted the template of points. In summary, this is not the method for your samples, I'm sorry.

For those reading this, I just want to be clear in what geomorph's 3D digitizing functions are doing. So the way that geomorph's buildtemplate function works is to take all of the vertices of the mesh (it does not downsample) and use the kmeans() function to find p centers from that set of vertices, where p is the number of semilandmarks chosen in buildtemplate. digitsurface then takes the template of semilandmarks and fixed landmarks exported from buildtemplate and uses the fixed landmarks on a second specimen to align and warp the template (via thin-plate spline). These functions require at least 4 fixed landmarks that are homologous on each sample. This is imperative. 

Emma
